records.name: Lambayeque
records.summary:
No trans-specific regional law, ordinance or enforcement pattern is documented for Lambayeque; what binds a visitor here is the national framework. In February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved the dictamen of bills 6506 and 8457, which bar trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex (narrow exceptions: custody, medical care, accompanying under-12s, the elderly or disabled) and prohibit ambiguous restroom signage; the plenary approved the fused text on 2 April 2025, waiving a second vote, and a university human-rights institute condemned Article 5.1 as legalized discrimination violating constitutional and inter-American equality guarantees.

Violence data is national only: the university TLGBI rights observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights-violation cases in 2020-2023 — over half of homicide victims trans women (30 of 54), 19 killings in 2023 alone — including a February 2023 case in which an extortion gang killed a trans sex worker in the capital. Enforcement would rest on individual staff checking IDs. The national machinery applies to Lambayeque in full.

The national machinery applies fully to Cajamarca.

records.name: Amazonas
records.summary:
Amazonas has no documented trans-specific regional law, ordinance or enforcement pattern; the national framework applies here as elsewhere in Peru. In February 2025 the congressional Women and Family Commission unanimously approved bills 6506 and 8457 barring trans people from public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than birth sex (narrow custody, medical and accompaniment exceptions; ambiguous signage banned); the plenary approved the fused text on 2 April 2025 without a second vote, and a university human-rights institute condemned Article 5.1 as legalized discrimination under constitutional and inter-American equality guarantees. Whether the law survived 2026 challenge or repeal cannot be confirmed from the available sources.

National monitoring is the only violence data: 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights-violation cases in 2020-2023 (30 victims trans women), including a February 2023 gang abduction and murder of a trans sex worker in the capital. No departmental breakdowns exist, so the national position stands for Amazonas unmodified.

records.name: El Callao
records.summary: No region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division - the research dossier lists it among the units with no sub-national signal, so the national evidence applies: the congressional Women and Family Committee approved bills banning trans people from public restrooms in early 2025 (floor vote pending), and the national university observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023, more than half of the homicide victims trans women (30 of 54). The absence of local findings reflects Peru's lack of hate-crime statistics rather than any positive local difference.
